select_cameras.title: Select Cameras
select_cameras.description: Choose which cameras from your CuboAI account to add. Nothing is added automatically — you can change this later in the integration Options.

config.title: Configure CuboAI Integration
config.description: Configure the alert and download behavior for your CuboAI cameras.

data.alerts_count: Number of alerts to retain in state attributes
data.max_saved_photos: Maximum number of downloaded photos to keep
data.hours_back: Time window to check for alerts (hours)
data.rtsp_port: RTSP port for the local camera stream
data.unifi_protect_enabled: Make a camera available to UniFi Protect (ONVIF)

data_description.rtsp_port: Port for the integration's own streaming engine. It self-heals — if the port you pick is already taken, it moves to the next free one automatically. Home Assistant's built-in go2rtc normally already uses 8555, so a default of 8557 here is expected and not an error.
data_description.enable_debug_logs: Turn on when reporting an issue. Writes full diagnostics for the whole integration: `cuboai_debug.log` (config folder, all integration messages), `custom_components/cuboai/bin/go2rtc.log` (streaming engine), `cuboai_last_alert_debug.log` (alerts), plus debug messages in the Home Assistant log. Log files rotate at 2 MB. Redact camera credentials before sharing — see the [debugging guide]({docs_url}).
data_description.unifi_protect_enabled: Lets UniFi Protect find this camera and add it as a third-party camera. In Protect, either turn on Settings → System → Discover Third-Party Cameras, or add it by address (shown as unifi_protect_address on the camera's WebRTC Stream sensor). One camera per Home Assistant host — Protect tells cameras apart by the host's network address. Protect plays H.264 only: a Cubo 3 needs 'Transcode these cameras to H.264' checked for it.
data_description.unifi_protect_password: Type this same username and password into Protect when it asks. Protect will not add a camera without a password.

data.alerts_count: Number of alerts to retain in state attributes
data.hours_back: Time window to check for alerts (hours)
data.h264_cameras: Transcode these cameras to H.264 (needed for HomeKit / HLS with H.265 cameras like Cubo 3)
data.rtsp_port: RTSP port for the local camera stream

data.unifi_protect_enabled: Make a camera available to UniFi Protect (ONVIF)

data_description.rtsp_port: Port for the integration's own streaming engine. It self-heals — if the port you pick is already taken, it moves to the next free one automatically. Home Assistant's built-in go2rtc normally already uses 8555, so a default of 8557 here is expected and not an error.
data_description.h264_cameras: Check a camera only if it is H.265/HEVC (e.g. Cubo 3 / SW05) and fails in HomeKit or the HA stream view with a 'demuxing timed out' error. Leave native-H.264 cameras (Cubo 2 / CB02) unchecked — transcoding uses extra CPU.
data_description.enable_debug_logs: Turn on when reporting an issue. Writes full diagnostics for the whole integration: `cuboai_debug.log` (config folder, all integration messages), `custom_components/cuboai/bin/go2rtc.log` (streaming engine), `cuboai_last_alert_debug.log` (alerts), plus debug messages in the Home Assistant log. Log files rotate at 2 MB. Redact camera credentials before sharing — see the [debugging guide]({docs_url}).
data_description.notify_on_engine_restart: The streaming engine is restarted automatically if it stops unexpectedly. Leave this on to be told when that happens — a crash used to be completely silent, and an engine that keeps dying is worth knowing about. Turn it off if you would rather not see the notification.
data_description.unifi_protect_enabled: Lets UniFi Protect find this camera and add it as a third-party camera. In Protect, either turn on Settings → System → Discover Third-Party Cameras, or add it by address (shown as unifi_protect_address on the camera's WebRTC Stream sensor). One camera per Home Assistant host — Protect tells cameras apart by the host's network address. Protect plays H.264 only: a Cubo 3 needs 'Transcode these cameras to H.264' checked for it.
data_description.unifi_protect_password: Type this same username and password into Protect when it asks. Protect will not add a camera without a password.
data_description.unifi_protect_port: Protect remembers this port when it adds the camera, so it is never changed automatically.
